The '''New Zealand Loyal Party''', also known as '''NZ Loyal''', is a registered, [[far-right politics in New Zealand|far-right]], [[Conspiracy theory|conspiracist]] [[political party in New Zealand]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/liz-gunns-new-zealand-loyal-election-results-which-electorates-gave-it-most-support/TUFSUDDCVRCYLGJ3DXZDHWGBXA/|title=Which electorate gave Liz Gunn's NZ Loyal party the most votes?|date=April 8, 2024|website=NZ Herald}}</ref> It was founded in June 2023 by [[anti-vaccination]] activist, and ex-[[TVNZ]] news presenter, [[Liz Gunn]].<ref name="shortlist" /> In the [[2023 New Zealand general election|2023 general election]] the party won 1.2% of the party vote and no seats. The party was deregistered in 2024 but remained active under the leadership of [[Kelvyn Alp]]. It was re-registered in August 2026.<ref name=":5">{{cite web |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2026/decisions-on-party-registrations-and-logos |title=Decisions on party registrations and logos |publisher=New Zealand Electoral Commission |date=5 August 2026 |access-date=5 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/election-2026-mariameno-kapa-kingis-new-party-approved-by-electoral-commission/DFSW2HKZVNDQZJPMGELK3NP3AY/ |title=Election 2026: Mariameno Kapa-Kingi's new party approved by Electoral Commission |publisher=New Zealand Herald |author=Julia Gabel |date=5 August 2026 |access-date=6 August 2026}}</ref>

== Policy positions (2023) ==
For the 2023 election campaign, the party described itself as opposed to "globalist interests" and in favour of "very little state interference in your life".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Manhire |first=Toby |date=2023-08-28 |title=Liz Gunn conspiracy party formally registered, targets 'deep state creatures' |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/live-updates/28-08-2023/liz-gunn-conspiracy-party-formally-registered-targets-deep-state-creatures |access-date=2024-04-09 |website=The Spinoff |language=en}}</ref><ref name="stuff-jul2024">{{cite web |last1=Arambepola |first1=Sanda |title=Liz Gunn's New Zealand Loyal Party is no more |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/350358887/liz-gunns-new-zealand-loyal-party-no-more |website=Stuff |access-date=29 July 2024 |date=29 July 2024}}</ref>

===Constitution===
NZ Loyal pledged to:
* Pull New Zealand out of international bodies including the [[United Nations]], [[World Economic Forum]], and [[World Health Organization]].
*  "Establish" a New Zealand constitution, despite the already existing, uncodified [[Constitution of New Zealand]].
* Oppose "race-based policies".
* Support limited, de-centralised government.<ref name="stuff-jul2024" /><ref name="policy-overview">{{cite web |title=Policy Overview |url=https://nzloyal.org.nz/pages/policy-overview |website=NZ Loyal |access-date=29 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231010062253/https://nzloyal.org.nz/pages/policy-overview |archive-date=10 October 2023}}</ref>
* Place a moratorium on immigration.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Scott |first1=Matthew |title=Who's who in the Election Fringe Festival |url=https://newsroom.co.nz/2023/09/26/whos-who-in-the-election-fringe-festival/ |website=Newsroom |access-date=31 July 2024 |date=26 September 2023}}</ref>

=== Enquires and investigations ===

Three separate policies promised investigations into the [[Reserve Bank of New Zealand]], the "Green Agenda", and the media.<ref name="policy-overview" />

===Health===
As a prominent anti-vaccination activist, Liz Gunn gave a health policy statement that opposed "covid kill shots" and repeated false claims about [[vaccines and autism]]. She called the government's response to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand|COVID-19 pandemic]] a [[Holocaust trivialization|"mini-holocaust"]]. She promoted conspiracy theories about [[big Pharma conspiracy theories|"big pharma"]] and the [[Federation of State Medical Boards]].

Gunn spoke in favour of [[Pseudoscience|pseudoscientific]] and [[Alternative medicine|alternative]] medicines and treatments including:
* [[Acupuncture]]
* [[Ayurvedic medicine]]
* [[Homeopathy]]
* [[Quantum healing]]
* Water therapy
* "Sound and light frequency therapy".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gunn |first1=Liz |title=Health |url=https://nzloyal.org.nz/pages/health |website=NZ Loyal |access-date=29 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231014011022/https://nzloyal.org.nz/pages/health |archive-date=14 October 2023}}</ref>

Other health-related policy positions opposed:
* [[Water fluoridation]]
* [[Genetically modified food|GMOs]]
* [[Anti-abortion movements|Abortion]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gunn |first1=Liz |title=Policy Position On Abortion |url=https://nzloyal.org.nz/pages/policy-position-on-abortion |website=NZ Loyal |access-date=29 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231010065228/https://nzloyal.org.nz/pages/policy-position-on-abortion |date=21 July 2023|archive-date=10 October 2023}}</ref>

===Education===
Leader Liz Gunn's policy statement on education promised to:
* End New Zealand's "morally bankrupt education system".
* Reduce the number of university students.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gunn |first1=Liz |title=Education |url=https://nzloyal.org.nz/pages/education |website=NZ Loyal |access-date=29 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231014082852/https://nzloyal.org.nz/pages/education |archive-date=14 October 2023 |date=31 August 2023}}</ref> 
* End "corrupt sex and gender 'education'" in schools.
* Teach children "objective morality".<ref name="policy-overview" />

===Economy===
NZ Loyal's economic policy statement was cast as a fight against the "Agenda 2030 plan to completely control every aspect of your lives", which is a conspiratorial view of the UN's [[sustainable development goals]].<ref name="econ-policy">{{cite web |last1=Gunn |first1=Liz |title=The Economy |url=https://nzloyal.org.nz/pages/the-economy |website=NZ Loyal |access-date=29 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231013235403/https://nzloyal.org.nz/pages/the-economy |archive-date=13 October 2023 |date=13 August 2023}}</ref> The party's policies included:

* Economic self-sufficiency and "full spectrum economic dominance" through the nationalisation of assets including "communication", transport infrastructure, water, the energy grid and power stations. 
* More oil and gas production, in response to the supposed environmental damage done by electric cars and batteries.<ref name="econ-policy"/>
* An end to [[Reserve Bank of New Zealand|reserve bank]] independence, which Gunn described as private ownership.
* Battling and defeating unnamed global bankers over government debt.<ref name="econ-policy"/>
* In a single line, both a "free and open market" and preferential use of local suppliers in housing and infrastructure. 
* Ending "excessive money printing" to prevent [[hyperinflation]] (which New Zealand has never experienced).<ref name="policy-overview" /> 
* A 1% transaction tax as part of a simplified tax code.<ref name="policy-overview" />

== 2023 general election ==
New Zealand Loyal received 1.2% of the party vote in the [[2023 New Zealand general election|2023 general election]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Zealand Election Results |url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/ |website=Election Results}}</ref> failing to reach the 5% required to gain seats in [[New Zealand Parliament|parliament]]. None of the party's 33 electorate candidates were successful.

=== Party list issues===
NZ Loyal intended to enter a 15-person party list, but failed to register most of those individuals in time. The party misunderstood different deadlines that applied to its party list and its "bulk information schedule" about constituency candidates.<ref name="law-assoc-oct23">{{cite web |last1=Wu |first1=Fiona |title=Liz Gunn-backed fringe party takes Electoral Commission to court over missed deadline |url=https://thelawassociation.nz/liz-gunn-backed-fringe-party-takes-electoral-commission-to-court-over-missed-deadline/ |website=The Law Association |access-date=24 October 2023 |date=20 October 2023}}</ref> Consequently, NZ Loyal's official party list contained Gunn, Peter Drew and Phillip George Engel, who left the party before voting opened.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023 General Election: Parties |url=https://vote.nz/2023-general-election/about/2023-general-election/parties |website=vote.nz |access-date=19 September 2023 |archive-date=10 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231210225952/https://vote.nz/2023-general-election/about/2023-general-election/parties/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=FreeNZ Media |title=MMP And Elections – Protest Party Vote | url=https://rumble.com/v3jjie6-mmp-and-elections-protest-party-vote-nz-loyal.html |website=Rumble |access-date=21 September 2023 |date=21 September 2023}}</ref> Had NZ Loyal passed the 5% [[Electoral threshold|vote threshold]] the remaining two candidates would have become MPs with the rest of the party's seats left vacant.

Gunn initially took responsibility for the administrative debacle, putting it down to "human error" within the party. Some days later she instead blamed "contradictory advice" from the Electoral Commission, which the party suspected may have been deliberate sabotage. Chief electoral officer Karl Le Quesne said that the Commission worked closely with all parties before and during the nomination period, that NZ Loyal submitted a list with three candidates within time, and that they had asked to add more people after the 14 September deadline.<ref name="shortlist">{{cite news |last1=Kelly |first1=Rachael |title=Liz Gunn's NZ Loyal to contest election with two on its party list |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/133005597/liz-gunns-nz-loyal-to-contest-election-with-two-on-its-party-list |access-date=25 September 2023 |publisher=Stuff |date=26 September 2023}}</ref>

At the High Court in Wellington on 6 October, the Electoral Commission argued that deadlines and time frames should be strictly observed. NZ Loyal argued that the court could simply declare that the list had been submitted before the deadline. The judge called this a "novel and creative" idea and said that, "If you leave it to the last minute and something goes wrong, the responsibility falls squarely on the party."<ref name="law-assoc-oct23" /> No changes were allowed to the party list.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liz Gunn's NZ Loyal takes Electoral Commission to court over missed deadline |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/133073445/liz-gunns-nz-loyal-takes-electoral-commission-to-court-over-missed-deadline |access-date=9 October 2023 |publisher=Stuff |date=6 October 2023}}</ref>

==Deregistration and rebuild (2024–26)==
On 29 July 2024 the party's registration was cancelled at its own request.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2024/new-zealand-loyal-no-longer-registered/ |title=New Zealand Loyal no longer registered |publisher=New Zealand Electoral Commission |date=29 July 2024 |access-date=29 July 2024}}</ref><ref name="stuff-jul2024" /> A few days later, on 1 August, Liz Gunn applied to personally trademark NZ Loyal's name, logo, and slogans for a range of uses including printed material, advertising, political fundraising, and political lobbying.<ref>{{cite web |title=1270333 - Trade Mark - New Zealand Loyal; NZL; Loyal; NZ Loyal; Loyal to you, Not to Them; NZLoyal; NZ LOYAL; Loyal to You, Not to Them; The People's Movement |url=https://app.iponz.govt.nz/app/Extra/IP/Mutual/Browse.aspx?sid=638596637534382688 |website=IPONZ |access-date=18 August 2024}}</ref> {{As of|2024|8|19}} her application is pending with the [[Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Trade mark detail - Case no. 1270333 |url=https://app.iponz.govt.nz/app/Extra/IP/TM/PublicSearch/PublicSearch.aspx?sid=638596636730704511&op=EXTRA_TM_PublicSearch&fcoOp=EXTRA_Default#markdetail |website=IPONZ |access-date=18 August 2024}}</ref>

In a series of back-and-forth videos over the following weeks [[Kelvyn Alp]] of [[Counterspin Media]], a far-right platform that had been involved and supportive in NZ Loyal's run for Parliament, accused Gunn of unilaterally shutting down the party in violation of its constitution, and of financial improprieties. Alp positioned himself as the main architect of the party's policies. Gunn responded to his claims by accusing him of stealing information from the party.<ref name=SSTAug2025/>

In November 2024 a new party board declared its intention to rebuild the party and fight the next election.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |last1=New Zealand Loyal Political Party |title=New Zealand Loyal Political Party Is Under New Management |url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2411/S00016/new-zealand-loyal-political-party-is-under-new-management.htm |website=Scoop |access-date=19 November 2024 |date=4 November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Block |first1=George |title=Liz Gunn fails in bid to dodge conviction for Auckland Airport assault |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/liz-gunn-fails-in-bid-to-dodge-conviction-for-auckland-airport-assault/BFCPKX5CWBABFDTWQ6QSK7UYQU/ |access-date=19 November 2024 |publisher=New Zealand Herald |date=19 November 2024}}</ref> At an AGM they elected Alp as leader, and Brenton Faithfull as party president.<ref name=SSTAug2025/> Also on the new "interim board" are Peter Verhoven and Marilyn Park.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Interim Board of New Zealand Loyal Political Party |url=https://newzealandloyal.com/the-board-of-nz-loyal |website=New Zealand Loyal |access-date=8 December 2024}}</ref>

Alp ran under the party banner in the [[2025 Tāmaki Makaurau by-election]] and gained 26 votes, the lowest of any candidate.<ref name="SSTAug2025">{{cite web |url=https://www.thepost.co.nz/politics/360787040/ghost-party-centre-bitter-political-feud |title=The 'ghost party' at the centre of a bitter political feud |publisher=Sunday Star-Times |date=17 August 2025 |access-date=17 August 2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250817095606/https://www.thepress.co.nz/politics/360787040/ghost-party-centre-bitter-political-feud |archive-date=17 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Results of the 2025 Tāmaki Makaurau By-election Official Count |url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2025-au5217 |access-date=18 September 2025 |work=[[New Zealand Gazette]] |date=17 September 2025}}</ref> Party founder and former leader Liz Gunn responded to Alp's candidacy by accusing him of "theft".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mitchell |first1=Charlie |title=The 'ghost party' at the centre of a bitter political feud |url=https://www.thepress.co.nz/politics/360787040/ghost-party-centre-bitter-political-feud |access-date=25 August 2025 |publisher=The Press}}</ref>

In June 2026, the party applied for re-registration.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 June 2026 |title=Three parties apply to register |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2026/three-parties-apply-to-register |access-date=12 June 2026 |website=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thepost.co.nz/politics/361023168/nz-loyal-makes-bid-political-return |title=NZ Loyal makes bid for political return |publisher=The Press |author=Federico Magrin |date=27 June 2026 |access-date=27 June 2026}}</ref> In August, the party's registration was accepted, however their application to register a party logo was denied.<ref name=":5" />

The leadership of New Zealand Loyal has been disputed since Alp became leader on 30 November 2024, after its initial deregistration. Gunn asserts that she remains the leader, and that the party under Alp is a "fake NZ Loyal."<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |url=https://www.facebook.com/NZLoyal/posts/pfbid0QyPe4cvQrtbm5zrQNL7kh5iag6S1uxBJ5kTbGzxpdy37utCDWrmu2zWkVDEzt291l|title=New Zealand Loyal's Facebook Post|date=15 July 2026|last=Gunn|first=Liz|access-date=15 July 2026|publisher=New Zealand Loyal|via=[[Facebook]]}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite news |title=The 'ghost party' at the centre of a bitter political feud |url=https://www.thepress.co.nz/politics/360787040/ghost-party-centre-bitter-political-feud |access-date=13 July 2026 |date=17 August 2025|last=Mitchell|first=Charlie|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250817095606/https://www.thepress.co.nz/politics/360787040/ghost-party-centre-bitter-political-feud|archive-date=17 August 2025|work=[[The Press]]|agency=[[Sunday Star-Times]]}}</ref> In response, the Alp-managed New Zealand Loyal stated that the members had taken back control of the party, and that Gunn's attacks on the New Zealand Loyal leadership was "convenient flip-flopping designed to sow chaos and derail re-registration."<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=16 July 2026|title=Liz Gunn's Sideshow Spectacle: Theatrical Distractions From A Party Reborn For Real Change|url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2607/S00099/liz-gunns-sideshow-spectacle-theatrical-distractions-from-a-party-reborn-for-real-change.htm|access-date=16 July 2026|publisher=New Zealand Loyal|via=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]]}}</ref>
